submission.natural_language_explanation: Layer-0 unigram (token-identity) detector: the current token alone sets the pole (token identity explains 91% of activation variance, 82% of the input attribution sits on the peak token itself, position ~1%), and it fires on a fixed, graded lexicon of specific vocabulary entries rather than on a topic - strongest on ' vit- ' forms (' vitamins' 1.12, ' Vitamin' 0.76, ' vitamin' 0.71, the pieces 'vit' 0.64 / 'itamin' 0.57), on Chinese health/importance/positive-affect words (维生素 1.35, 重视 0.95, 兴奋 0.81, 自信 0.72, 重要 0.72, 营养 0.71, 乐观 0.65), and at 0.35-0.75 on the Latinate stems ' important/importance', 'etermin/determin(ation/ant)', 'optim(ism/istic/ization)', 'abil/abilit/stabil/instability/rehabilitation' and the word-internal piece 'ital' (vital, revitalisation, hopital), plus camelCase identifiers built from them (legalArgumentException 0.94, .dropout 0.70, addPreferredGap 0.64, ToggleButton 0.50). It is lexical, not conceptual or orthographic: near-synonyms spelled as different tokens stay at the 0.00-0.16 baseline ('significant' 0.06, 'crucial' 0.16, 'health' 0.16, 'nutrient' 0.15, 'hope' 0.07, 'ability' 0.00 while the piece 'abilit' gives 0.46, 'optimal' 0.05 while 'optimization' gives 0.45) and the same letters inside another token never fire ('gravity' 0.01, 'activity' 0.01, 'hospital' 0.00 versus the piece 'ital' 0.40), while a trigger token fires from any sentence and any position (' important' gives 0.44-0.72 across frames, ' vitamins' 1.12-1.17); only about 0.5% of the tokens of ordinary mixed web text cross the 0.25-of-max threshold, so the mechanism is retrospective, not lookahead (its Jacobian-lens list is incoherent, kurtosis 3.4).
